page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors. It features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 188.0 GB, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the QEMU hypervisor. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests placing in the top 25% of results. Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics, similarly rank in the top 25%. In database and memory write operations, the server demonstrates high efficiency, achieving 64.55 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and scoring in the top 25% for Passmark database operations and large block memory write bandwidth of 95.71 GB/sec. Conversely, memory read bandwidth and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall within the average middle 50% range. Large-model LLM inference speeds also register in the average tier, with a 70B model processing prompts at 12.32 tokens per second.

The ccx63 server offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated CPU cores with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This configuration delivers high compute-per-resource value for multi-threaded workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The inclusion of a 960 GB local NVMe SSD enhances its suitability for data-intensive tasks. Based on its benchmark profile, this server is suited for database operations, software compilation, Redis caching layers, and small-scale language model inference.
